messages.subject: boxplot: how to get vertical lines at the end of the whiskers?
parts:
Dear expeRts,

Is there a way to obtain vertical bars at the end of the whiskers in a
ggplot2 boxplot (similar to the standard boxplot)? (Although I tried,
I could not find a solution in the forum)

qplot(factor(cyl), mpg, data = mtcars, geom = "boxplot")


Cheers,

Marius

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: boxplot: how to get vertical lines at the end of the whiskers?
parts:
Hi:

(a) The definition of the boxplot in geom_boxplot() is the same as
that in graphics::boxplot().
(b) If you save a boxplot() to an object, it will return a list whose
first component is a matrix that includes the positions of the
whiskers.

That information can be transferred to a data frame which can be used
as input to geom_segment() to produce whiskers for the boxplots.
Here's a reproducible example using the built-in InsectSprays data:

bpstat <- boxplot(count ~ spray, data = InsectSprays)
str(bpstat) # the stats component contains the positional info
bpstat$stats
whiskers <- with(bpstat, data.frame(spray = names,
lower = stats[1, ],
upper = stats[5, ]))

ggplot(InsectSprays) + geom_boxplot(aes(x = spray, y = count)) +
geom_segment(data = whiskers, aes(x = as.numeric(spray) - 0.1,
y = lower,
xend = as.numeric(spray) + 0.1,
yend = lower)) +
geom_segment(data = whiskers, aes(x = as.numeric(spray) - 0.1,
y = upper,
xend = as.numeric(spray) + 0.1,
yend = upper))

Longer whiskers are obtained by increasing the value from 0.1 to
whatever suits you.

HTH,
Dennis
